# Worked examples: the three games

Part of [vehicle components](README.md). Each example is built and tested as a synthetic fixture in
`libs/blackbox-components/src/tests/` (invented names and numbers, no game data); the test names are given. What each game
really has is cited; what is assumed is marked **[assumed]**.

## The 2005 game

*Test fixtures: `tests/nfs2005.rs`.* Every stock car offers the same slots, and a stock car's definition is **generated by an
adapter from the install's tables**, not written by hand: the parts database and the car's customization catalog
(`nfsmw_data::car::customization::Catalog`) give the model parts, the paints and the vinyls; `PerformanceCatalog::read` gives
the performance ladders. The adapter lives in `crates/nfsmw-data` (stage 4 of [the plan](../../plans/vehicle-components.md)).

### What the current code is, and where it goes

| Today | Where | In the new model |
|---|---|---|
| `Category` (9) and `Selection.parts: [Option<u32>; 9]` | `customization.rs` | slots `body`, `spoiler`, `hood`, `roof`, `rims`, `paint`, `tint`, `rim_paint`, `vinyl`; the pick holds the component. The arrays disappear |
| `rim_color`, `vinyl_colors: [_; 3]`, `vinyl_color_parts` | the same | `rgb` inputs of `rim_paint` and `paint`; the three vinyl channels as slots `vinyl_colour_1..3` whose components are the palette entries |
| `decals: [[Option<u32>; 8]; 6]` | the same | 48 slots `decal.<zone>.<n>` in group `decals` |
| `PerformancePackage { levels: [u8; 7], junkman: u8 }` | `physics/performance/` | seven slots with a ladder each and seven junkman slots (below) |
| `GaugeSelection`, `ExhaustSelection` | `garage/mod.rs` | slots in groups `hud` and `exhaust` (checked in stage 4) |
| `aero_changed` unlocks aero tuning | `garage/parts.rs` | the spoiler and body kit components set the flag `aero.tuning_unlocked` |
| fitted wheel part per axle (slots 66, 67) | `slot::FRONT_WHEEL`, `REAR_WHEEL` | one slot `rims`; the component shows both wheel parts |

### Ids and the save

A model part is the component `nfsmw:part/<name hash, 8 hex digits>`: the identity the original save already stores. A
selection read from a stock save maps part hashes to component ids and back **without loss**, so the original save format
stays the file format of the 2005 garage (`Selection` of the new model is derived from it and written back to it). Stock
parts are the defaults. A part that no slot of this car accepts (the parts database lists compatible parts per slot through
`SlotTypes`) does not appear in `accepts`.

### Performance packages

The 2005 game does not store a stat table per level. It stores, per car and category, *a number of levels* and two endpoint
attribute collections, and **resolves the level by interpolation** ([performance-upgrades.md](../performance-upgrades.md)).
That resolution stays in the game's tables; the component carries only the level:

```toml
[[component]]
id = "nfsmw:perf/engine/2"
name = "engine.stage2"
tier = 2
effects = [{ kind = "param", key = "package.engine", op = "set", value = 2 }]
```

- The slot `engine` of a car whose vehicle record says three engine upgrades accepts levels 0..3 (`CategoryOptions::max_level`); a car with
  no nitrous upgrades has a slot that accepts only level 0, or no slot at all. **Per-car ladder length is per-vehicle
  availability.** A category whose endpoints are missing from the install has only level 0 (`missing_endpoints`).
- Resolution reads `package.engine` from `ParamTable::set_value` and feeds `PerformancePackage.levels`; `performance::apply`
  does the rest, unchanged. The proof of equivalence is the existing test suite of that module.
- **Junkman** is a second slot per category, `engine.junkman`, with components `off` and `on` (`package.engine.junkman` flag).
  Its eligibility is `junkman_available`: the category must have modifiers, and either its stock package is present
  (`stock_present`) or a level above 0 is installed. So the slot has no `when` for a category whose stock package exists, and
  `when = [tier induction >= 1]` for induction or nitrous on a car that has none from the factory. The shop's "Max + Junkman"
  button is `normalize` over "all top tiers, all junkman on".
- **Prices** come from the frontend tables into `price`; **trade-in** (a quarter of the installed part's price, none for
  performance) stays the shop's rule.

### Looks

```toml
[[component]]
id = "nfsmw:paint/gloss"        # one per finish/preset part; custom RGB is an input
effects = [{ kind = "surface", target = "body", finish = "gloss", colours = { base = "colour" } }]
[[component]]
id = "nfsmw:part/0a1b2c3d"      # a body kit
effects = [{ kind = "part", show = ["slot23:0a1b2c3d"], hide = ["slot44:11223344"] }]   # hides this car's stock spoiler part
```

(the adapter owns the part-id namespace: `slot<N>:<hash>` is "the part with that hash in slot N"). A wide kit that
carries its own wing excludes the spoiler: `is_not { slot = "bodykit", any_of = [...] }` on the spoiler offer, or `hide` on the
kit; both are tested (`wide_kit_and_gt_spoiler_exclude_each_other`). The turbo that needs a tuned engine, and the junkman
box that exists only with a turbo, are `turbo_needs_an_engine_tier_and_a_reset_follows_the_engine` and
`junkman_slot_exists_only_with_the_turbo`.

## The 2012 game

*Test fixtures: `tests/nfs2012.rs`.* What the repository **knows**: the 2012 game keeps `PowerTrain`, `Nitrous`, `Body`,
`Chassis` and `Tyre` upgrade lists per car (`CarUpgrade`, [code]), two gearboxes in the handling definition (stock and
upgraded), and no looks to choose beyond paints and liveries ([chameleon-customization.md](../../formats/chameleon-customization.md)).
What it does **not** know: the contents of the upgrades (the 8,304-byte `PerformanceUpgrades` record is not decoded). The
tiers below are the brief's description (body: stock, lightweight, impact resistant, offroad; tyres: stock, slick, offroad,
inflatable, drift) **[assumed]** with invented numbers, to show the model, not to describe the game.

```toml
[[component]]
id = "body.lightweight"
tier = 1
effects = [
  { kind = "param",     key = "stats.mass_kg", op = "mul", value = 0.9 },
  { kind = "behaviour", domain = "damage.profile", select = "fragile" },     # a lighter body also changes the damage table
]
[[component]]
id = "tyres.inflatable"
when = [{ kind = "is", slot = "body", any_of = ["body.offroad"] }]
effects = [
  { kind = "part",      show = ["tyre.inflatable"] },
  { kind = "param",     key = "stats.front_tire_grip", op = "mul", value = 0.9 },
  { kind = "param",     key = "buoyant", op = "set", value = true },
  { kind = "behaviour", domain = "tyre.compound", select = "inflatable" },
]
[[component]]
id = "tyres.drift"
effects = [
  { kind = "behaviour", domain = "tyre.compound",  select = "drift" },
  { kind = "behaviour", domain = "handling.model", select = "drift" },        # the game picks its drift handling
  { kind = "param",     key = "drift_assist", op = "set", value = true },
]
```

Each of these **both** changes a number and a behaviour, in one component, so the vehicle cannot be left with slick numbers
and offroad handling: the pair is installed or removed together. The tests cover a body and a tyre combining
(`a_body_and_a_tyre_change_numbers_and_behaviour_together`), a rule between tiers (offroad bodies exclude slicks and allow
inflatables), the reset when the body changes (`changing_the_body_resets_the_tyres_that_needed_it`) and a conflict note.

How the 2012 content mod uses it (stage 5): `mods/nfsmw-2012-content` writes `components/upgrades.toml` and a `[[slot]]` list per
car (the 93 cars share their slots through one `slot_set`), with the base `[stats]` it already writes
(`src/stats.rs`) as the stock numbers. Its `[performance]` multipliers stay what they are: the user's conversion-time tuning
of the stock numbers, applied before the components. The game's two gearboxes are a pair of `stats.gear_ratios` lists
(`stock`, `upgraded`) and a `transmission` tier that `set`s the list.

## RIDE 6

*Test fixtures: `tests/ride6.rs`.* What the repository **knows**: the bindings tables `graphics/Bindings/Bike/*` give one row
per part kind per vehicle (`CHASSIS`, `TYRE_SIZES`, `FRONT_TYRES`, `BACK_TYRES`, `RIMS`, `BRAKES_KIT`, `BRAKES_KIT_OVERRIDE`,
`EXMANIFOLD`, `MUFFLER`, `BARPADS`, `HANDGUARDS`, `CHAIN`), each row pointing at one data asset (mesh, material); a bike
whose table has no row for it simply has no such part (the KTM 450 SMR has no `CHAIN` rows, most road bikes no bar pad;
[ride6-bikes.md](../../modding/ride6-bikes.md), [ride6-bikes-batch.md](../../modding/ride6-bikes-batch.md)); the physics data has
`TuningComponentData` rows that change a member path by a multiplier or an addition, and upgrades (`Upgrade_Motard`,
`QuickShifter-RM`, `LaunchControl-RM`) that change members of the resolved vehicle data. The importer today reads only the
**stock** rows. Whether the tables carry alternative rows per bike (other mufflers, forks) is **[assumed]** from the brief and
is the first thing stage 5 inventories.

### Per-bike availability = the rows

The importer builds each bike's `[[slot]]` list from the tables that have rows for it:

| Table | Slot | Components (one per row) | Effect of the alternative |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MUFFLER` + `EXMANIFOLD` | `exhaust` | stock, aftermarket... | `part` (swap the silencer and header solids), `param` (power), `behaviour` `exhaust.sound` and `exhaust.flames` |
| `BARPADS` | `bar_pad` | stock, none | `part` show/none |
| `HANDGUARDS` | `hand_guards` | stock, none | `part` |
| `CHAIN` | `chain`, `chain_colour` | stock, race | `part`; the colour is a `surface` on target `chain` with an `rgb` input |
| `RIMS`, `BRAKES_KIT` | `rims`, `brakes` | rows | `part` (wheel solids), `param` (brake torque, unsprung mass) |
| the fork/shock data | `suspension` | stock, stiffer... | `part` (the steered fork solid) + `param` (`bike.front_suspension.*`) |

The KTM 450 definition lists `exhaust`, `bar_pad`, `fork` and no `chain`; the Panigale V4 S lists `exhaust`, `chain`,
`chain_colour` and no `suspension`. `a_slot_the_bike_does_not_have_is_refused_not_ignored` shows a peer or a save that names
a slot the bike lacks is refused, and `the_chain_colour_exists_only_with_the_race_chain_and_resets_without_it` shows the
dependent slot (colour only with the coloured chain) appearing, vanishing and resetting with its parent.

### An exhaust change, end to end

```toml
[[component]]
id = "ride6:exhaust.race"
tier = 1
price = 900
effects = [
  { kind = "part",      show = ["muffler.race"] },                       # the silencer solid; the stock one is shown by exhaust.stock
  { kind = "param",     key = "bike.engine.torque_scale", op = "mul", value = 1.04 },
  { kind = "behaviour", domain = "exhaust.sound",  select = "race" },    # a sound set (ride6-bikes-sound.md); the game maps the name
  { kind = "behaviour", domain = "exhaust.flames", select = "race" },    # flame profile for backfire/NOS
]
# in the bike's manifest
[parts."muffler.race"]
solid   = "PANIGALE_KIT00_MUFFLER_RACE"
markers = [{ name = "RIGHT_EXHAUST", position = [-0.88, -0.14, 0.33], direction = [-1, 0, 0] }]
```

- **Visual:** the stock bike draws `muffler.stock` (shown by `exhaust.stock`); the race exhaust shows `muffler.race` instead.
  The importer must therefore write the silencer and header as **their own solids per component** (today they are merged into
  the body solid, [ride6-bikes.md](../../modding/ride6-bikes.md)); the meshes are already separate in the export
  (`exmanifold369_369`, `muffler369`).
- **Flames and pipe position:** the tail pipe marker belongs to the part, so the flame (`exhaust-flames.md`) follows the
  muffler that is drawn. Today the importer derives the outlet from the silencer mesh (`mods/ride6-bikes/src/exhaust.rs`); it does the
  same per component.
- **Performance:** a multiplier on the engine torque key. In the real data this is a `TuningComponent` multiplier on a
  member path; the key is that path.
- **Sound:** `exhaust.sound = race` selects a sound set of the bike; the bike's `[car_sound]` / engine sound tables list sets
  by name ([ride6-bikes-sound.md](../../modding/ride6-bikes-sound.md)); a set that is not listed falls back to the stock set
  and the option is not offered for that bike.
- **Compose:** `an_exhaust_swaps_the_muffler_and_changes_power_sound_and_flames` checks parts, sound, flames and the
  numbers; `a_vehicle_prices_a_component_its_own_way` checks the per-bike price of one shared component.

### Limits of this example

- The **chain and sprockets are part of the skinned chassis mesh** for the KTM
  ([ride6-bikes.md](../../modding/ride6-bikes.md)). A `chain` slot that shows and hides parts needs the chain as its own
  mesh; where the data does not give one, the slot can only recolour a material (`surface`) or must not be offered.
- The bike's tuning menu (suspension preload and damping sliders) is continuous player tuning, not components, and stays
  outside this model, as the 2005 tuning screen does.
